Audit1682: reserved Jetson capsule durability and firmware consumption

Generation is offline. Every case starts not_run. This supplements the separate
2341 rootfs-only plan; that plan supplies pinned identity, binaries and the
read-only snapshot helper, not evidence that a capsule has ever applied. No
commands below are run by generation. Run this only on reserved serial @SERIAL@.
Generate on the host with:
  python3 .github/regression-coverage/manual/jetson-capsule-rehearsal.py inventory.json /absolute/new-output-directory

Preparation and admission

1. Supply inventory JSON with ab_plan pointing to the exact generated2341
   evidence.json. Keep all its hashed inputs, generated files and pinned updater
   checkout available. Supply archive, descriptor, payload_inspection and capsule
   paths for ONE new capsule-bearing .wendy release. The descriptor contains url,
   sha256, size_bytes, storage, artifact_name and artifact_version. The inspection
   must independently bind artifact_sha256, rootfs_sha256, agent_sha256,
   updater_sha256, bootloader_marker_present:true, capsule_path exactly
   /opt/nvidia/UpdateCapsule/tegra-bl.cap, capsule_sha256, capsule_size_bytes and
   reviewer. Inspect the actual rootfs marker /var/lib/wendyos/update-bootloader;
   manifest bootloader_update alone does not select this path. The generator
   verifies archive/compressed-payload hashes but does not mount/decompress the
   rootfs or authenticate NVIDIA's capsule signature. Producer inspection and
   vendor signature/board compatibility qualification are required separately.

2. Supply transition fields from_firmware, to_firmware, from_esrt_version,
   to_esrt_version, esrt_firmware_guid, vendor_qualification,
   antirollback_compatible:true and recovery_independently_verified:true. Also
   supply transition_record, recovery_record, power_isolation_record and
   authorization_record files, boot_seconds (60..900), power_off_seconds (10..120).
   These are independently reviewed lab records, never inferred from filenames.
   The expected transition is @FROM@ -> @TO@, ESRT firmware class @GUID@.
   A no-op/reinstalled version cannot prove capsule consumption. Do not downgrade
   firmware or alter ESRT/EFI variables to manufacture a transition. Review secure
   boot/signing policy, ratchets and lowest_supported_version before admission.

3. Recovery must already be qualified for the exact ECID, carrier, root disk and
   firmware family. Preserve an independently verified, vendor-supported recovery
   image/tool version and the physical recovery procedure, storage backup and
   serial console. Firmware updates can advance anti-rollback state: a filesystem
   backup does not guarantee firmware rollback. Never reuse the same forward
   transition twice by assuming reflashing rootfs restores old firmware. Cases A
   and B require independent reserved baseline boards, or an explicitly qualified
   recovery that restores the complete permitted initial firmware state. Otherwise
   run one case and retain the other not_run.

4. Owner authorization must cover the exact physical board/storage, firmware
   transition, possible recovery write and the separate acknowledged-stage power
   interruption. Identify every power feed including USB, batteries and PoE;
   isolate only the reserved target. The power record names the physical connector
   or exact controlled outlet, human operator and independent loss-of-power
   indication. No generic network switch API is supplied. Maintain stable power
   throughout firmware programming. Do not interrupt NVIDIA capsule processing.
   No production application, model, credential or unrelated volume is removed.

5. Before each case run the prepared2341 snapshot helper from the local serial
   console, with its exact config and observed initial slot. Use its 180-second
   outer bound. Require exact DT serial/SoC, GPT APP/APP_b/ESP roles and UUIDs,
   parent disk serial, active root/boot chains, binary hashes, healthy Agent and
   no pending deployment. Agent SHA256 @AGENT@; updater SHA256 @UPDATER@.
   Preserve boot ID, serial UEFI banner, OS version, firmware version and L4T.
   Existing pending deployment is a STOP: the volatile-zero Orin pending-readiness
   exception remains unfixed; do not erase state or invoke mark-good to bypass it.

6. Read firmware observations locally, without changing them:
     date -u
     cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
     timeout 15 nvbootctrl get-current-slot
     timeout 15 nvbootctrl -t rootfs get-current-slot
     timeout 15 nvbootctrl dump-slots-info
     timeout 15 find /sys/firmware/efi/esrt/entries -maxdepth 2 -type f -print
   From the enumerated entries, identify exactly one fw_class matching @GUID@;
   retain fw_class, fw_version, lowest_supported_fw_version, last_attempt_version
   and last_attempt_status from that entry. Names/entries unavailable on this
   firmware mean the corresponding ESRT acceptance remains pending, not zero.
   Preserve the firmware banner as independent version evidence. Record the raw
   bytes/attributes of the enumerated OsIndications-* efivar, without writing it:
     timeout 15 find /sys/firmware/efi/efivars -maxdepth 1 -name 'OsIndications-*' -print
   Read the one actual path with od -An -tx1. The first four bytes are attributes;
   FILE_CAPSULE_DELIVERY is bit2 of the following little-endian uint64 value.
   Do not confuse attributes with the value or assume a missing variable is zero.

7. Resolve ESP /dev/disk/by-partuuid/@ESP@ against the validated GPT layout.
   Identify any existing mount using:
     timeout 15 findmnt -rn -S /dev/disk/by-partuuid/@ESP@ -o SOURCE,TARGET,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
   If already mounted, inspect that exact mount and do not remount/unmount it.
   If unmounted, the owner may create a fresh private directory with mktemp -d
   /tmp/ci1682-esp.XXXXXXXX and mount ONLY that partition there, read-only:
     ESP_VIEW=$(mktemp -d /tmp/ci1682-esp.XXXXXXXX)
     timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 15s mount -t vfat -o ro /dev/disk/by-partuuid/@ESP@ "$ESP_VIEW"
   ESP_VIEW must be the exact newly created directory, never an existing path.
   Independently verify findmnt --mountpoint "$ESP_VIEW" reports the expected
   resolved device and ro,vfat before reading. After observations, unmount only
   this newly owned mount with the same timeout and rmdir only the empty owned
   directory. An uncertain mount/unmount completion is a stop; leave the directory
   for exact-owner recovery, never recursively delete it. No fsck/repair/write.
   Capture whether EFI/UpdateCapsule/TEGRA_BL.Cap already exists. A stale capsule
   or active FILE_CAPSULE_DELIVERY bit invalidates the clean baseline; use qualified
   recovery rather than deleting someone else's staged update.

Case A: actual Agent update and firmware consumption

8. Start continuous serial capture BEFORE the generated agent_capsule_update.
   This exact CLI command uploads the pinned Agent and requests the immutable
   capsule artifact. Observe installation for at most @INSTALL@ seconds; retain
   failure/stall evidence and inspect the exact target if that window expires. Do
   not start a second writer or cut power to interrupt an in-progress installation.
   It must run in text mode because --artifact-url rejects
   --json. Record installed/source OS version and actual reboot path. On 0.17.0
   and 0.18.0 the Agent logs the WDY-2200 systemd handover; newer/unknown versions
   use sync followed by immediate reboot. A modern-only run does not exercise
   the older clean-handover case. Historical affected releases require their own
   qualified forward transition/recovery, not a spoofed OS-version file.

9. Retain the actual staging/reboot transcript. Do not race an ESP mount against
   the running installer or attempt to pause firmware programming. Within @BOOT@
   seconds observe a NEW boot ID, actual UEFI capsule processing, firmware @TO@,
   exact ESRT class and expected new fw_version/last_attempt_version, success
   last_attempt_status, and the expected newly installed root/boot chain. Correlate
   the old/new versions and capsule identity with the reviewed transition. An old
   status0, a changed rootfs alone, or the updater accepting a successful boot
   with unreadable ESRT is insufficient for this stricter physical acceptance.

10. Require target rootfs version @VERSION@, the installation's verified payload
    digest @PAYLOAD@ and status/history matching that artifact/slot. Do not hash a
    live writable root partition and compare it to the producer image after boot.
    Capture bounded current-boot Agent/updater journals and check commit completes
    with no pending state or rollback. Repeat the read-only baseline observations.
    Firmware normally CONSUMES the staged capsule; record file/indication state,
    but absence alone is neither success nor loss. A remaining capsule with no
    fresh firmware transition fails this case. Once stable, run generated
    console_reboot_after_success and require a second new boot ID, persistent new
    firmware/root identity and healthy Agent within @BOOT@ seconds.

Case B: storage durability after acknowledged staging, before reboot

11. Restore the separately qualified initial state or use the second reserved
    baseline board and regenerate its exact identity plan. Repeat steps5..7.
    Through local serial console invoke generated console_stage_without_reboot.
    Pinned wendyos-update install writes/stages and returns WITHOUT rebooting.
    Observe at most @INSTALL@ seconds. Wait for successful exit and the pending
   swapped state; retain complete
    terminal output and generated console_status. An interrupted/failed install
    is not eligible for the power cut. Do not invoke Agent's rebooting update in
    this case, and do not have any automatic reboot service running concurrently.

12. Before any reboot, observe the exact staged ESP capsule by step7: size @SIZE@
    and SHA256 @CAPSULE@ at EFI/UpdateCapsule/TEGRA_BL.Cap; record OsIndications
    FILE_CAPSULE_DELIVERY, boot_attempted, bl-version-before and pending state.
    Require the correct target slot/artifact/payload. Close the owned read-only
    view before proceeding. The updater has already called file fsync, rename and
    filesystem syncfs before acknowledging staging. A mount/unmount or diagnostic
    read may change cache/writeback timing; this case tests post-acknowledgement
    cold-start persistence, not loss of an unflushed Agent write window.

13. With the OS still running at the staged prompt, no reboot requested and no
    capsule programming underway, the authorized operator removes ONLY the exact
    recorded target power feeds. Record external evidence that power was lost;
    leave off for @OFF@ seconds. Restore stable power once. Record uninterrupted
    serial boot and repeat steps9..10, including fresh firmware application and
    second-boot persistence. If a reset/firmware transition already began, do NOT
    make the cut; mark this attempt not_run and retain the timing evidence.
    On boot failure stop at @BOOT@ seconds and use the independently qualified
    recovery procedure. Do not loop uncontrolled power cuts or rewrite EFI state.

Remaining timing-specific acceptance — explicitly pending

14. Agent sync-to-reboot fault injection and the 60-second stuck-clean-shutdown
    fallback are separate cases. They need a qualified external trigger/capture
    rig with exact board/outlet ownership, measured trigger latency, proof of the
    sync/reboot boundary, and protection against cutting power once firmware
    programming starts. No such rig or command is supplied here. Keep both cases
    not_run until that exact reviewed procedure exists. Do not stop PID1, hang
    filesystems, unload storage drivers or disable watchdogs on an ad-hoc target.

15. An omit-Agent-sync negative control against this CURRENT updater can still
    succeed because its copyFileSync already fsyncs/renames/syncfs the ESP. That
    success cannot prove the Agent fix irrelevant, and failure must not be forced
    by casually removing updater durability calls. A historical affected stack
    requires exact Agent/OS/updater source+binary identities, qualified compatible
    capsule transition and independently authorized recovery. Keep original
    fault sensitivity pending unless such a discriminating control is recorded.

For each executed case retain source/binary/artifact/capsule hashes, identity and
pre/post snapshots, external power timings, serial transcript, ESRT/current boot
logs, actual exit results, recovery outcome and reviewer. Record failed separately
from not_run; generation itself never updates a physical result to passed.
